newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins steady, trade thin after holidays.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins steady, trade thin after holidays.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds were little changed in quiet post-holiday trading on Sunday and dealers said news Russia's long-awaited Eurobond issue was due on November 21 to 25 failed to spark much activity.
November 7 to 9 were holidays in Russia, marking the 1917 Bolshevik Revolution, while Sunday is a working day.
Finance Minister Alexander Livshits said on Saturday Russia would issue its first Eurobond between November 21 and 25, for up to $500 million.
"There is nothing new in what he said, so nobody cared," one dealer said.
Dealers said just a few deals had been struck through the day, with many operators stopping work after lunch.
